title: [Stage 1] Agree notification types, channels and priorities
body:
Lock down what the system must deliver before anyone builds.

**Done when**
- [ ] The five notification types in `contracts/openapi.yaml` are confirmed or changed by the whole team
- [ ] Each type has an agreed default for in-app, email and push
- [ ] Priority levels (urgent, normal, low) and what each means are written down
- [ ] Decision recorded in `docs/` and linked here

**Notes**
SMS is out of scope — there is no free provider. The adapter interface leaves room for it later.

title: [Stage 2] Confirm the UI template and install it
body:
We have no designer, so the template is the design decision. Make it once, then never revisit it.

**Done when**
- [ ] Team confirms shadcn/ui (or picks an alternative from `docs/UI-TEMPLATE.md`) — decide in one meeting, not over a week
- [ ] Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind scaffolded in `/frontend`
- [ ] `npx shadcn@latest init` run and committed
- [ ] Components added: button badge popover dropdown-menu scroll-area separator skeleton sonner switch label card select alert form table avatar
- [ ] Dark mode working through the theme tokens
- [ ] A screenshot of the running blank app posted in this issue

**Blocks everyone else on the frontend. Do this first.**

title: [Stage 2] App shell, routing and layout from the template
body:
Strip TailAdmin's free React dashboard down to the shell we actually need.

**Done when**
- [ ] Top bar (where the bell will live) and sidebar
- [ ] Routing set up with a page per route: inbox, preferences
- [ ] Responsive down to 360px — sidebar collapses on mobile
- [ ] TailAdmin's demo charts, tables and widget pages deleted, not left lying around
- [ ] `src/features/notifications` and `src/features/preferences` folders created empty, so Pulse and Beacon can start

title: [Stage 2] Shared components and the screen conventions
body:
The rule that replaces having a designer: nobody hand-rolls what the template already has.

**Done when**
- [ ] `NotificationIcon` component mapping each of the five types to an icon and colour
- [ ] `EmptyState`, `ErrorState` and `LoadingSkeleton` components everyone reuses
- [ ] `RelativeTime` component ("2 min ago")
- [ ] A short `frontend/README.md` section: use theme tokens, never raw hex; shared components go in `src/components` and Prism reviews them
- [ ] Pulse and Beacon have both read it

title: [Stage 3] Finalise the API contract
body:
`contracts/openapi.yaml` and `contracts/realtime-events.md` are the agreement that lets frontend and backend work in parallel. Review them together and sign off.

**Done when**
- [ ] Every endpoint reviewed by at least one frontend person
- [ ] Socket.IO event payloads confirmed
- [ ] The mock server runs: `npx @stoplight/prism-cli mock contracts/openapi.yaml --port 4010`
- [ ] Merged to main — after this, changes need a PR with both a backend and a frontend approval

title: [Stage 3] Architecture diagram and queue decision
body:
Write down how the pieces fit, so all seven hold the same picture.

**Done when**
- [ ] Diagram: producer API, queue, workers, channel adapters, database, Socket.IO gateway
- [ ] BullMQ + Redis confirmed as the queue (see `docs/STACK.md`)
- [ ] The job payload shape agreed between Bell, Relay and Ember — this is the contract the three of you meet at
- [ ] Diagram committed to `docs/`

title: [Stage 3] Free-tier accounts and shared environment secrets
body:
Nobody should be blocked waiting for a database URL.

**Done when**
- [ ] Neon (Postgres) project created, connection string shared with the team privately
- [ ] Upstash (Redis) database created
- [ ] Brevo account created and the sender address verified
- [ ] Firebase project created for Cloud Messaging
- [ ] All keys added as GitHub repository secrets (Settings → Secrets → Actions)
- [ ] `.env.example` updated if any variable name changed

**Never commit a real key. `.env` is in `.gitignore` — keep it that way.**

title: [Stage 3] CI pipeline running on every pull request
body:
**Done when**
- [ ] `.github/workflows/ci.yml` lints the OpenAPI contract
- [ ] Backend and frontend jobs install, test and build
- [ ] CI is a required status check on `main`
- [ ] A deliberately broken PR is opened to prove CI catches it, then closed
- [ ] CI finishes in under 5 minutes, so nobody is tempted to skip it

title: [Stage 4] Database schema and Prisma migrations
body:
Tables: users, notifications, preferences, devices, delivery_attempts.

**Done when**
- [ ] `backend/prisma/schema.prisma` covers all five tables
- [ ] Indexes on `(userId, createdAt)` and `(userId, read)` — the notification list depends on them
- [ ] `delivery_attempts` records channel, status, error and attempt number
- [ ] First migration runs cleanly against a fresh database
- [ ] Seed script creates a test user with sample notifications

**Blocks Relay and Ember. Do this first on the backend.**

title: [Stage 4] Express app skeleton and auth middleware
body:
The shell every other backend issue builds inside.

**Done when**
- [ ] Express app with error handling and request logging
- [ ] JWT middleware for browser routes
- [ ] `x-service-key` middleware for `/internal/*`
- [ ] Errors come back in the `Error` shape from the contract
- [ ] `GET /health` returns 200

title: [Stage 4] Producer endpoint: POST /internal/notifications
body:
Accept a notification request, check preferences, put a job on the queue.

**Done when**
- [ ] Validates the body against the contract
- [ ] Looks up the user's preferences and drops channels they have switched off
- [ ] Returns 202 with `{ jobId, status }` where status is queued, duplicate or suppressed
- [ ] `idempotencyKey` seen before returns `duplicate` without queueing again
- [ ] Returns in under 100ms — the actual sending is the worker's job

title: [Stage 4] Read endpoints: list, unread count, mark read, mark all read
body:
The four endpoints the notification panel calls.

**Done when**
- [ ] `GET /notifications` with cursor pagination and the `status=unread` filter
- [ ] `GET /notifications/unread-count`
- [ ] `PATCH /notifications/:id/read` returns the updated notification and fresh count
- [ ] `PATCH /notifications/read-all`
- [ ] Each marks-read call emits the matching Socket.IO event to that user's room
- [ ] A user can never read another user's notifications — test this

title: [Stage 5] BullMQ queue and worker skeleton
body:
The heart of the system.

**Done when**
- [ ] Queue connects to Redis from `REDIS_URL`
- [ ] Worker picks up jobs and logs them
- [ ] Three priority levels map onto BullMQ priorities
- [ ] Worker runs as its own process (`npm run worker`), not inside the API
- [ ] Graceful shutdown: finish the current job, then exit

title: [Stage 5] Retries, exponential backoff and the dead-letter queue
body:
What makes the system reliable rather than merely working.

**Done when**
- [ ] Failed jobs retry 5 times with exponential backoff starting at 2s
- [ ] A job that exhausts its retries moves to a dead-letter queue instead of vanishing
- [ ] Every attempt writes a `delivery_attempts` row with the error
- [ ] A permanent failure (invalid email address) fails fast with no retries
- [ ] Rate limiting so we stay inside Brevo's 300/day free tier
- [ ] Idempotency: the same job running twice sends one notification, not two

title: [Stage 5] Socket.IO gateway for in-app delivery
body:
**Done when**
- [ ] Socket.IO server with JWT verification in the handshake
- [ ] Each connection joins the room `user:<userId>`
- [ ] Worker emits `notification:new` to that room after saving to the database
- [ ] An unauthorised handshake is rejected with `unauthorized`
- [ ] Matches `contracts/realtime-events.md` exactly
- [ ] Two browser tabs stay in agreement when one marks a notification read

title: [Stage 5] Scheduled and delayed jobs
body:
Needed for quiet hours and for any reminder-style notification.

**Done when**
- [ ] A job can be queued with a delay
- [ ] A job delayed past a quiet-hours window fires at the right local time
- [ ] Delayed jobs survive a worker restart
- [ ] Ember can call this from the channel layer without knowing how BullMQ works

title: [Stage 6] The Channel interface and the in-app channel
body:
One interface that every channel implements, so adding SMS later is a new file, not a rewrite.

**Done when**
- [ ] `Channel` interface: `send(notification, user)` returning success or a typed failure
- [ ] A failure is marked either retryable or permanent — the retry logic depends on this distinction
- [ ] In-app channel writes to the database and hands off to Relay's gateway
- [ ] A registry maps channel name to implementation, so the worker never uses a switch statement

title: [Stage 6] Email channel with Brevo, plus templates
body:
**Done when**
- [ ] Brevo adapter implementing the `Channel` interface
- [ ] One HTML template per notification type, with a plain-text fallback
- [ ] Unsubscribe link pointing at the preferences page
- [ ] A send failure throws the right failure type so retries work
- [ ] Test email actually arrives in a real inbox, and looks right on a phone

title: [Stage 6] Push channel with Firebase Cloud Messaging
body:
**Done when**
- [ ] FCM adapter implementing the same `Channel` interface
- [ ] Sends to every registered device token for the user
- [ ] An invalid or expired token is deleted rather than retried forever
- [ ] Browser push works end to end on one machine
- [ ] Deep link opens the right page when the notification is tapped

title: [Stage 6] Preferences and device endpoints, with quiet hours
body:
**Done when**
- [ ] `GET /preferences` returns sensible defaults for a user who has never saved any
- [ ] `PUT /preferences` validates every type and channel key
- [ ] Quiet hours stored with a timezone and applied when deciding to send
- [ ] A low-priority notification inside quiet hours is delayed, not dropped; urgent goes through
- [ ] `POST /devices` registers a push token, replacing a duplicate rather than adding a second row

title: [Stage 7] Typed API client and data layer
body:
Both frontend feature folders depend on this, so it comes before the screens.

**Done when**
- [ ] Client generated from `contracts/openapi.yaml`, so types cannot drift from the contract
- [ ] TanStack Query set up for caching and refetching
- [ ] `VITE_API_URL` switches between the mock server (4010) and the real backend (4000)
- [ ] Auth token attached to every request
- [ ] Beacon confirmed it works for the preferences endpoints too

title: [Stage 7] Notification bell and panel
body:
Build against the mock server — do not wait for the backend. Use the template's `popover`, `scroll-area` and `badge`; do not hand-roll them.

**Done when**
- [ ] Bell with unread badge, hidden at zero
- [ ] Dropdown panel listing notifications, newest first
- [ ] Unread items visually distinct; type icons from Prism's `NotificationIcon`
- [ ] Clicking an item marks it read and follows its link
- [ ] 'Mark all as read' works
- [ ] Empty, loading and error states use Prism's shared components
- [ ] Infinite scroll or a 'load more' button using the cursor

title: [Stage 7] Socket.IO client and live toasts
body:
Toasts come from Sonner, which ships with the template. Stacking and auto-dismiss are already handled — do not rebuild them.

**Done when**
- [ ] Socket connects with the JWT and reconnects on its own
- [ ] `notification:new` prepends to the list, raises the badge and fires a Sonner toast
- [ ] Urgent toasts stay until dismissed; others fade after 5 seconds
- [ ] After a reconnect, the client calls `GET /notifications` once to catch up
- [ ] `notification:read` from another tab updates this one

title: [Stage 7] Preferences page
body:
Use the template's `switch`, `table`, `card` and `form` components.

**Done when**
- [ ] Grid of notification types by channel, using `switch`
- [ ] Quiet hours picker with a timezone
- [ ] Saves through `PUT /preferences` with a clear success state
- [ ] Unsaved changes warn before navigating away
- [ ] Works on a phone-width screen

title: [Stage 7] Full notifications page and browser push opt-in
body:
The panel shows the recent few. This is the 'view all' page, plus the permission flow.

**Done when**
- [ ] Full-page list with filters by type and by unread
- [ ] Pagination or infinite scroll
- [ ] Browser push permission prompt, asked at a sensible moment rather than on first load
- [ ] Granted permission registers the device via `POST /devices`
- [ ] A clear explanation shown if the user has blocked notifications in their browser

title: [Stage 7] Sign-in screen and auth flow
body:
Everything else assumes a signed-in user with a JWT, so somebody has to build that.

**Done when**
- [ ] Sign-in form using the template's `form`, `input` and `card`
- [ ] Token stored and attached by Pulse's API client
- [ ] Protected routes redirect to sign-in when there is no valid token
- [ ] Sign-out clears the token and disconnects the socket
- [ ] An expired token is handled without the app crashing

Keep it simple — this is not the point of the project, it just has to work.

title: [Stage 8] Integration: swap mocks for the real API
body:
Expect mismatches here. That is what this stage is for.

**Done when**
- [ ] Frontend points at the real backend
- [ ] Full flow works: event → producer API → queue → worker → channel → panel
- [ ] Live toast arrives without a page refresh
- [ ] Every mismatch between the contract and the implementation is fixed in one or the other
- [ ] A demo script exists so anyone on the team can reproduce the flow

title: [Stage 9] Load test and failure simulation
body:
**Done when**
- [ ] 1,000 jobs queued at once; the queue drains cleanly and nothing is lost
- [ ] Email provider outage simulated: jobs retry, then land in the dead-letter queue
- [ ] Redis restart simulated mid-run: no jobs lost
- [ ] Worker killed mid-job: the job is retried, not silently dropped
- [ ] Results written up in this issue with the numbers

title: [Stage 9] Backend unit and integration tests
body:
**Done when**
- [ ] Tests for the producer, preference filtering, quiet hours and idempotency
- [ ] Each channel adapter tested against a fake provider
- [ ] Users cannot read each other's notifications — test proves it
- [ ] Tests run in CI in under two minutes

title: [Stage 9] Frontend tests and cross-device checks
body:
**Done when**
- [ ] Component tests for the bell, panel and toasts
- [ ] Dropped WebSocket reconnects and catches up — tested
- [ ] Chrome, Firefox and Safari checked
- [ ] Works on a real phone, not just a resized window
- [ ] Keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels on the bell and panel

title: [Stage 9] Consistency and accessibility pass
body:
The job that used to belong to a designer. One person walks every screen.

**Done when**
- [ ] Every screen uses theme tokens — no raw hex anywhere, checked with a grep
- [ ] Dark mode correct on every screen
- [ ] Spacing and type sizes consistent between the three feature folders
- [ ] Colour contrast meets WCAG AA
- [ ] Any component duplicated across features is moved into `src/components`
- [ ] Five people outside the team try the flow; confusion noted and turned into issues

title: [Stage 10] Deploy backend, worker and frontend
body:
**Done when**
- [ ] API deployed to Render's free tier
- [ ] Worker running as its own service, not inside the API
- [ ] Frontend on Vercel or Netlify, deploying from `main`
- [ ] Neon, Upstash, Brevo and FCM connected through environment variables
- [ ] Migrations run automatically on deploy
- [ ] CORS and the Socket.IO origin allow the production domain
- [ ] Render's free-tier sleep behaviour documented in the README so nobody is caught out at the demo

title: [Stage 10] Monitoring and a queue health view
body:
**Done when**
- [ ] Sentry free tier catching errors on backend and frontend
- [ ] Queue depth, processing time, failure rate and dead-letter size visible somewhere
- [ ] An alert when the dead-letter queue grows past a threshold
- [ ] A short runbook in `docs/`: what to check first when notifications stop arriving

title: [Stage 11] Retrospective and next-version backlog
body:
**Done when**
- [ ] Team retro: what worked, what did not, what to change
- [ ] Findings from Stage 9 turned into issues
- [ ] Candidates considered: notification grouping, daily digests, SMS, a mobile app
- [ ] README updated with the current state and how to run everything
